1.w: A good name is to be chosen rather than great wealth, good favor more than silver or gold.

2.w: The rich and the poor are met together; the Lord is the Creator of them both.

3.w: A shrewd person saw danger and hid himself, but the naive passed on by and paid for it.

4.w: The reward for humility and fearing the Lord is riches and honor and life.

5.w: Thorns and snares are in the path of the perverse, but the one who guards himself keeps far from them.

6.w: Train a child in the way that he should go, and when he is old he will not turn from it.

7.w: The rich rule over the poor, and the borrower is servant to the lender.

8.w: The one who sows iniquity will reap trouble, and the rod of his fury will end.

9.w: A generous person will be blessed, for he has given some of his food to the poor.

10.w: Drive out the scorner and contention will leave; strife and insults will cease.

11.w: The one who loves a pure heart and whose speech is gracious —the king will be his friend.

12.w: The eyes of the Lord watched over a cause and subverted the words of the treacherous person.

13.w: The sluggard has said, “There is a lion outside! I will be killed in the middle of the streets!”

14.w: The mouth of an adulteress is like a deep pit; the one against whom the Lord is angry will fall into it.

15.w: Folly is bound up in the heart of a child, but the rod of discipline will drive it far from him.

16.w: The one who oppresses the poor to increase his own gain and the one who gives to the rich —both end up only in poverty.

17.w: Incline your ear and listen to the words of the wise, and apply your mind to my instruction.

18.w: For it is pleasing if you keep these sayings within you, and they are ready on your lips.

19.w: So that your confidence may be in the Lord , I hereby make them known to you today—even you.

20.w: Have I not written thirty sayings for you, sayings of counsel and knowledge,

21.w: to show you true and reliable words, so that you may give accurate answers to those who sent you?

22.w: Do not exploit a poor person because he is poor and do not crush the needy in court,

23.w: for the Lord will plead their case and will rob the life of those who are robbing them.

24.w: Do not make friends with an angry person, and do not associate with a wrathful person,

25.w: lest you learn his ways and entangle yourself in a snare.

26.w: Do not be one who strikes hands in pledge or who puts up security for debts.

27.w: If you do not have enough to pay, your bed will be taken right out from under you!

28.w: Do not move an ancient boundary stone that was put in place by your ancestors.

29.w: You have seen a person skilled in his work— he will take his position before kings; he will not take his position before obscure people.
